title: Passkeys: registration, sign-in and management
description: Add WebAuthn passkeys as the default way to sign in. Storage: a credentials table (credential id, public key, sign counter, transports, backup flags, user-given name, created and last-used times) and a stable random user handle per user. Flows: enrol a passkey when accepting an invite, during first-run setup, and from a 'Sign-in methods' page; sign in with a discoverable credential (no username typed) with a username-first path as fallback; rename and remove passkeys; never allow removal of a user's last sign-in method. The relying-party ID and origin come from the public URL (WI-126). Challenges are single-use, short-lived and bound to the browser session. The login page leads with 'Sign in with a passkey' and offers the password form as a secondary option only when the user or instance allows it. Use the maintained github.com/go-webauthn/webauthn library; read its current documentation before coding rather than relying on remembered API shapes.

recommended_model.name: Fable 5.2
recommended_model.rationale: Security-critical protocol work where subtle mistakes (origin checks, challenge reuse, enumeration, lockout) are easy to make and hard to spot.

acceptance_criteria: A user can enrol more than one passkey, name them, see when each was last used, and remove any but their last sign-in method
Sign-in works with a discoverable credential on current Safari (iOS/macOS), Chrome (Android/desktop) and Firefox, and degrades to a clear message where WebAuthn is unavailable
Challenges are random, single-use, expire within minutes, and are verified against the configured origin and relying-party ID
A cloned-authenticator signal (sign counter going backwards) is logged and surfaced to administrators
First-run setup (WI-117) offers passkey enrolment for the first administrator
Successful passkey sign-in creates the same session as password sign-in, with the same expiry rules
Login throttling covers passkey attempts without letting an attacker lock out a named user
No WebAuthn JavaScript is loaded from a third-party host

notes: Request user verification as 'preferred' and resident keys as 'required' for enrolment so discoverable sign-in works.
Do not reveal whether a username exists in the username-first path.
Local development on http://localhost is a valid WebAuthn origin; document the dev settings.

testing_requirements: Unit tests with the library's test helpers / a software authenticator

context.user_story: As a captain, I want to sign in with my phone's fingerprint or face instead of remembering a password.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
